reasons.C: Keeps the author's communal 'we', period diction and semicolon-joined clauses, and ends on a dry, ironic turn; sentences run somewhat longer than the passage's, but tone and stance fit best.
reasons.D: The short declaratives and gentle, deadpan irony match the passage's rhythm well, but the steady first-person 'I' and the thick 'I do not' anaphora move away from the author's plural stance and lean toward caricature.
reasons.B: Period feel and semicolons are right, but a personal 'I' narrator and a few set-piece flourishes ('hissed from the stage') make it more essayistic and less plainly assertive than the author.
reasons.A: Modern diction ('peaked', 'our nerves still remember', 'a business or a patient') and a contemporary explanatory manner; the rhythm and register read as a present-day writer, not the author.
